- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days post-spike.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and smooth decay curve.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; apply mean reversion heuristic: anchor forecast to 30-day moving average of recent 10–15 days.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >+5% per week), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–3% per week for 3–5 days ahead.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend, model overestimates; apply downward adjustment of 3–5% per week for 3–5 days ahead.
- Model underperforms in “late window” (last 10–15 days of 30d forecast) — especially when true outcome is volatile — apply smoothing with exponential decay (alpha=0.3) to reduce noise.
- When sentiment is absent or neutral, model should not assume sentiment-driven momentum — treat as baseline, no amplification.
